title: Personal and Enterprise Digital Twin Architecture Contract
thesis: The core product is a governed platform for managing separate Personal and Enterprise Digital Twins, with authorized relationships between them.
definition: A Digital Twin is a persistent, time-aware, evidence-linked computational representation of an entity's state, context, goals, relationships, behavior and outcomes that can be updated by events and used to support human decisions.
non_definition: A Digital Twin is not a static profile, user record, CRM contact, directory entry, database row, avatar or collection of attributes without state transitions and feedback.

twin_types.name: Personal Digital Twin
twin_types.purpose: Help a person understand, manage and develop identity, capabilities, goals, wellbeing, relationships and progress.

twin_types.name: Enterprise Digital Twin
twin_types.purpose: Help an organization understand, manage and improve its structure, capabilities, resources, processes, goals, risks and outcomes.

required_core.name: Entity Identity
required_core.question: What entity does this twin represent?

required_core.name: State Model
required_core.question: What is true about the entity now?

required_core.name: Event History
required_core.question: What changed, when and because of what event?

required_core.name: Context Model
required_core.question: Under what situation, environment or conditions is the state interpreted?

required_core.name: Goals and Intentions
required_core.question: What is the entity trying to achieve?

required_core.name: Evidence and Provenance
required_core.question: How do we know the state or capability claim?

required_core.name: Relationships and Dependencies
required_core.question: What other entities, resources or systems affect the twin?

required_core.name: Behavior and Transition Rules
required_core.question: How can the state change when events or actions occur?

required_core.name: Actions and Feedback
required_core.question: What action was taken and what outcome followed?

required_core.name: Governance and Access
required_core.question: Who may view, update, infer or act on the twin, for what purpose?

required_core.name: Time and Versioning
required_core.question: How did the twin evolve and what was true at a prior time?

cross_twin_relationship.name: Authorized Personal-Enterprise Relationship
cross_twin_relationship.purpose: Represent the governed relationship between a person and an enterprise without merging their identities or unrestrictedly copying their data.
rules: Personal and Enterprise Twins remain separate systems of representation.
The relationship has its own purpose, permissions, validity period and audit trail.
Personal data is not automatically owned by the enterprise.
Enterprise data is not automatically visible to the person beyond the authorized view.
Cross-twin actions require human or governed organizational authorization.
Sensitive personal data is excluded unless explicitly required, consented and controlled.

profile_database: May not preserve event causality or provenance
Does not require a state-transition model
Does not inherently model goals, behavior or outcomes
Does not inherently support simulation or feedback
digital_twin: Updates through events and validated evidence
Preserves provenance and confidence of claims
Models goals, context, relationships and dependencies
Defines state transitions and behavior rules
Connects actions to outcomes and feedback
Supports human decisions, scenarios or governed agent assistance
Enforces identity, access, purpose and audit controls

mvp_boundary.rule: Do not build both full twin types at once.
mvp_boundary.first_vertical_slice: One bounded Personal Digital Twin use case with identity, consent, state, events, evidence, one goal and one human decision flow.
mvp_boundary.enterprise_twin: Conceptual and contract-level until an enterprise use case and buyer are validated.
mvp_boundary.student_profile: A possible initial Personal Digital Twin vertical slice; it is not the complete Personal Digital Twin.
